comments.author: @blackmanblue8937
comments.text: Every human service job has it's own stresses and challenges to our level of tolerance.  Nursing and doctoring has the high stress of people being in severe need of life changing and life maintaining help, that must be provided by competent, calm, and compassionate people.  Three things are changing that are making their working environment harder to exist in:  people, policies, and personal internal stress.  Some people in normal circumstances when they are feeling great, but they are absolute a-holes toward everyone when they are sick.  Some recently established health care policies that hospitals and clinics force nurses and doctors to accept as part of their interaction with patients,  facilitate conflicts and confusion in the knowledge, training, and natural awareness of people of what is human nature and what is human biology; none of which they can openly speak about in the workplace without being "outed" by a healthcare worker.  Some doctors and nurses are great at doing the nuts and bolts of the job, but don't have the personal skills required to contort into an acceptable caricature of themselves to gain the acceptable of patients and other healthcare workers.  To quit nursing or doctoring, is the easiest path of escaping the "job hell" situation, but moving into a smaller, slower-paced, healthcare space to work in is also a viable option.  This is also happening in all jobs/careers in which their is para-professional training and certification is worked TO WORK IN HUMAN SERVICES JOBS/CAREERS.  No judgement on anyone who leaves their career to maintain their peace, mental health and physical health.  Special note:  population growth also leads to more people needing to be seen in hospitals and health clinics; people are exhausted by the overworking that happens to them.  Creating that situation for them to work in is just wrong.  My thoughts and prayers are with them.
